The annotated solution has been saved to `answer.json`.

The annotation preserves every original C token and the original `//@ assert(y == 0)`, adding:
- A function contract (`requires x >= 0; assigns x, y; ensures x == 0;`)
- Loop annotations (`loop invariant y - x == j - i; loop assigns x, y; loop variant x;`)

The invariant captures that both `x` and `y` are decremented equally, so their difference stays constant (`j - i`). At loop exit `x == 0`, giving `y == j - i`, and inside `if(i == j)` that yields `y == 0` — proving the assertion. The `requires x >= 0` makes `loop variant x` valid for termination.
